messages.author: Yami
messages.content: Question: Can bots use lorebook entries to refer to other lorebook entries?

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content: No

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content: You can use lorebook entries to refer to things in the lorebook, but not other entries themselves.

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content: For example, if you have the keyword DUSK and the keyword DAWN and in DUSK's entry it lists it as "the opposite of dawn", the bot won't then read DAWN's context entry as well.

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content: It'll only read the context for DUSK.

messages.author: Kasztan
messages.content: How does it work? I created a bot and lorebook. How do I connect them? The bot and lorebook.

messages.author: Kasztan
messages.content: How do I get this lorebook to work on a single bot? I don't fully understand the mechanics of it.

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content:
TL;DR

Lorebooks act like REMINDERS to a bot.

When a KEYWORD is said, the bot gets reminded of the context behind that keyword.

That context stays in the memory for 4 messages.

ACTIVATION (you or bot)

Message 1
Message 2
Message 3
Message 4

DEACTIVATION (bot forgets context)

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content:
So say you list a character's name like JOHN SMITH as the KEYWORD, and the context for that name is

"Deceased"

When the name JOHN SMITH gets said, the bot is reminded "oh yeah, he's dead"

messages.author: JaaShooUhh
messages.content: That way the bot doesn't bring him back to life over and over again.
